Data.title: Alarming Chart for Bitcoin (BTC)! According to CryptoQuant, Analysts Are Increasingly Turning Bearish! Here Are the Details
Data.body: The declines in Bitcoin and altcoins, the Democratic victory in the US midterm elections, increasing inflationary pressures, and rising expectations of a Fed interest rate hike are leading analysts to adopt a cautious stance. At this point, data shared by CryptoQuant indicates a significant shift in analyst expectations regarding Bitcoin’s future. The CryptoQuant data shows a seriously negative turn in the market outlook. Top 10 Analysts More Cautious About Bitcoin! According to research shared on CryptoQuant’s Analyst Consensus platform, the market optimism (sensitivity scores used by CryptoQuant) of the top 10 Bitcoin analysts with the highest historical accuracy rates has dropped from 79 to 58 in the last month. The decline in optimism among other analysts was more limited, falling from 77 to 68. The study compared the forecasting performance of 66 analysts followed for a year. It noted that the top 10 analysts made more accurate assessments than others, particularly during downturns. While the accuracy scores of both groups were equal at 84 during bull markets, the top 10 analysts scored 48 during bear markets, while the other analysts scored 36. CryptoQuant also revealed that out of 149 analysts who provided clear opinions in the last 7 days, 88 indicated a bullish position and 59 indicated a bearish position. This distribution shows that approximately 62% of analysts expect a rise, and the majority still maintain a bullish outlook. However, the weakening of bullish views compared to previous periods indicates a decrease in optimism in the market. It is not specified how many analysts still hold a positive view, which led to the drop from 88. According to CryptoQuant, this distribution doesn’t indicate that Bitcoin has definitively entered a bear market, but rather that analyst opinions have shifted significantly towards a downward trend. Analysts say that the shift in market sentiment is influenced by outflows from ETFs, inflation concerns, and the weakening of the Nasdaq index. CryptoQuant also highlighted the decline in the Analyst Consensus Index, which tracks analysts’ market assessments. According to CryptoQuant data, the index fell from -1.0 in the first week of November to -1.8 in just one week. This indicates a significant shift towards pessimism and bearish sentiment regarding the Bitcoin market. According to CryptoQuant, a positive market sentiment is indicated when the index’s 90-day average is above zero, a +1.5 level represents significant optimism, and a +2 level represents optimism above the usual levels. Conversely, negative values below zero indicate an expectation of a decline. According to the data, a level of -1.5 is considered a clear bear market expectation. At this point, the current decline of the index to -1.8 reveals that the pessimism among analysts has exceeded the threshold of a clear bear market. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Bitcoin dismal descent continues: Is $69K next?
Data.body: The Bitcoin price seems to be in a downward spiral that it just cannot break out of. Every single upward rally stops short of the previous one and every correction goes further down than the one before. Next stop the top of the 2021 bull market at $69K? $BTC price begins to breakdown Source: TradingView The slide continues. The $BTC price did break up from the descending wedge pattern , but as per usual the price rolled over and has come back to test the upper trendline of the wedge. If it does, it probably wouldn’t take long for the $BTC price to descend to $69K , a price it was struggling to get through as long ago as 2021. Data.title: Major Crypto Crime Task Force Launched by TRON, Tether, and Chainalysis
Data.body: TRON , Tether, and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis have joined forces to develop a major crypto crime task force against cryptocurrency-related crime, launching a new initiative focused on identifying suspicious transactions and disrupting illicit financial networks. The three companies announced the creation of the Digital Crime Task Force (DCTF) on November 12. Its primary objective is to detect and disrupt illegal activity involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the TRON blockchain, with a particular focus on helping authorities freeze suspicious assets before criminals can move them elsewhere. The initiative comes as crypto-related fraud, hacking, and money laundering continue to challenge the digital asset industry. It also follows the recent dissolution of an earlier crime-fighting partnership involving TRON, Tether, and TRM Labs, raising questions about whether the new collaboration can deliver more effective results. New Digital Crime Task Force Targets Illicit USDT Activity The DCTF aims to improve coordination between blockchain companies and law enforcement agencies by combining transaction monitoring, investigative intelligence, and faster responses to suspicious activity. A central priority is shortening the time between identifying potentially criminal transactions and taking action against them. This could allow authorities and participating companies to intervene before funds are transferred across multiple wallets, converted into other assets, or moved through different blockchain networks. TRON founder Justin Sun emphasized the importance of protecting users who rely on USDT for everyday financial activity, including payments, business transactions, and international transfers. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also highlighted the growing sophistication of cryptocurrency crime. He said the company had already frozen more than $7 billion connected to illicit activity while cooperating with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries. The new initiative will focus on several categories of financial crime, including investment fraud, romance scams, cryptocurrency hacks, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations , and other illicit financial networks. Chainalysis will contribute blockchain intelligence and investigative capabilities to help identify suspicious activity and support enforcement efforts. AI-Powered Scams Increase Pressure on Crypto Security The announcement arrives as artificial intelligence makes certain types of financial fraud more sophisticated and profitable. According to figures highlighted by Chainalysis, AI-enabled scams were 4.5 times more profitable than conventional schemes in 2025. Impersonation scams also increased by more than 1,400% year over year, demonstrating how quickly criminals are adopting new technologies to target victims. AI tools can help fraudsters create convincing messages, impersonate trusted individuals or organizations, and operate scams at a larger scale. This creates additional challenges for crypto companies attempting to identify suspicious behavior before victims lose their funds. The task force’s approach reflects a shift toward earlier intervention rather than relying exclusively on investigations after a crime has occurred. By combining transaction monitoring with cooperation between industry participants and authorities, the organizations hope to identify criminal networks and restrict access to illicit funds more quickly. New Partnership Follows the Collapse of Previous Crime-Fighting Alliance The launch also comes shortly after the reported dissolution of the T3 Financial Crime Unit, an earlier initiative established by TRON, Tether, and TRM Labs in September 2024. That major crypto crime task force was created to investigate illicit transactions involving USDT on TRON and support efforts to freeze suspicious assets. Binance later joined the initiative, which announced that it had helped freeze approximately $250 million in illicit assets. However, the alliance reportedly struggled with slow response times and coordination problems before being discontinued. The development raised questions about the ability of major crypto companies to maintain effective cooperation when responding to increasingly complex financial crimes. The new DCTF therefore represents another attempt to strengthen cooperation between major blockchain and stablecoin industry participants. Its success will depend on whether the organizations can improve operational coordination and respond quickly enough to prevent suspicious funds from disappearing across multiple networks. Can the New Task Force Make Crypto Transactions Safer? TRON, Tether, and Chainalysis are positioning the Digital Crime Task Force as a more proactive approach to combating cryptocurrency-related crime. With AI-powered fraud becoming increasingly sophisticated, faster detection and cooperation with law enforcement could become essential to protecting digital asset users. Nevertheless, the major crypto crime task force faces a significant challenge: identifying suspicious transactions is only part of the process. Turning that information into timely asset freezes and successful investigations will determine whether the partnership can make a measurable difference. Do you think the new task force can improve the industry’s ability to prevent crypto-related money laundering? And will closer cooperation between blockchain companies and law enforcement make stablecoins safer for everyday users?

Data.title: Pundit Says 2029 Looks Like the Year for a Major XRP Price Boom. Here’s why
Data.body: Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz recently opened up about his personal relationship with risk and XRP, and the community is paying attention. Your Friend Blondie (@myfriendblondie) believes XRP is heading for a major price surge in 2029. She is using his comments to make her case. Schwartz shared that he has not bought XRP in a long time. He described himself as “very uncomfortable with risk” and confirmed he has sold nearly all of his digital assets . He still holds Ripple stock, and he called that alone “more risk than I wish I had.” Your Friend Blondie reads these comments not as a condemnation of XRP but as a reflection of his personal risk tolerance. She believes the 2029 timeline remains intact. David @JoelKatz from @Ripple is pretty much saying $XRP isn’t going to take off anytime soon. I feel like he’s giving us a heads-up about what’s to come. 2029 is looking like the year for a major XRP price boom. pic.twitter.com/dQiccCsfvs — 𝓨𝓸𝓾𝓻 𝓯𝓻𝓲𝓮𝓷𝓭, 𝓑𝓵𝓸𝓷𝓭𝓲𝓮 (@myfriendblondie) November 10, 2026 Schwartz on Risk A community member told Schwartz that life is a risk. Schwartz agreed but explained his own position. He acknowledged that “nearly every risk I’ve taken in the crypto space has worked out well for me.” He recognizes logically that he should take more chances, but says he cannot get comfortable taking many risks . Schwartz Still Holds Millions of XRP One community member brought up something important. He referenced recent comments from Schwartz confirming that he still holds approximately 3 million XRP, down from a high of around 26 million. Schwartz also disclosed moving from roughly 1,500 BTC to 1 BTC and from around 40,000 ETH to 6 ETH. These are significant reductions, but 3 million XRP is still a substantial position. The XRP Community Is Split Not everyone shares Your Friend Blondie’s optimism. One community member expressed skepticism about the 2029 timeline. He argued that predictions like this shift regularly and that enthusiasm around any specific year is not grounded in evidence. He noted that a similar target year was being discussed back in 2023. Another member projected XRP staying under $1 by 2029 under most scenarios, with $27 as a best-case figure only if full adoption occurs. He noted that Bitcoin would need to reach $200,000 to $300,000 for XRP to potentially ride that momentum back to around $3. Why 2029 Still Has Believers Sentiment in the XRP community is currently poor. The price is down , and patience is running thin. Your Friend Blondie’s position is that this is precisely when conviction is built. Schwartz’s transparency about his holdings and risk tolerance does not signal the end of XRP’s story. She sees the 2029 window as real, and she is watching closely. Disclaimer : This content is meant to inform and should not be considered financial advice. Data.title: MSCI Confirms Strategy and Metaplanet Removal at November’s Rebalance
Data.body: TL;DR: MSCI has confirmed that Strategy and Metaplanet will leave relevant equity indexes after the November 30 close. The change redirects benchmark-tracking funds’ shareholdings; it does not itself require either company to sell Bitcoin. The uncertainty over whether MSCI would remove two prominent Bitcoin treasury companies has become a dated implementation event. Its November review places Strategy among US standard-index deletions and Metaplanet among Japanese small-cap deletions. That gives investors a specific question to assess: how will demand for these companies’ shares change when funds following the affected benchmarks rebalance? It is a different question from whether the companies remain able or willing to hold Bitcoin. The November lists make the decision concrete MSCI’s standard-index changes name Strategy A in the US deletions column. Its small-cap changes list Metaplanet for removal in Japan. The provider’s review announcement , released November 11, says changes take effect after trading closes on November 30. Investors therefore have a timetable rather than a consultation proposal. The distinction matters because a possible future exclusion and an announced rebalance can produce different positioning decisions, even if market participants have been preparing for the outcome. For a fund whose mandate closely follows an affected index, holding an excluded stock may create a mismatch with that mandate. Other shareholders can make different decisions based on valuation and company strategy. That difference is why the rebalance identifies a channel of potential selling pressure without measuring the final market impact. A broader test of operating activity In its final methodology announcement , MSCI describes a first screen for substantial operating assets, followed by five financial ratios for companies that fail that initial test. Four flagged ratios can make a security ineligible, with timing rules intended to limit unnecessary turnover. This is an index eligibility judgment. It should not be read as a determination that Bitcoin ownership is unlawful, or as a regulatory order to unwind a treasury. A benchmark provider decides what belongs in a particular investment universe; that decision can still carry significant commercial consequences for an excluded company. Strategy disputes the premise and the scale Strategy’s consultation response argues that its Bitcoin activity is an operating business and criticizes MSCI’s approach. The company also says MSCI-linked funds held roughly 13 million of its shares, or 3.1% of basic shares outstanding, at the time of its response. Those are Strategy’s estimates and arguments, not an independent forecast of the eventual selling. Current holdings, trading ahead of the rebalance and the methods individual funds use will affect how the change reaches the market. A holding estimate should not be presented as a guaranteed dollar outflow. Why Bitcoin investors are watching the equity market The potential connection runs through financing. If a treasury company can issue shares on attractive terms, it may use the proceeds to acquire Bitcoin. Less demand for those shares could make that route more expensive or less appealing. The outcome depends on valuation, alternative financing and management’s allocation decisions. NewsBTC’s coverage of Strategy’s latest Bitcoin purchase and preferred-share repurchases shows why those choices need to be examined together. Raising capital does not mean every dollar automatically becomes a Bitcoin purchase. The distinction also helps separate this event from redemptions in spot Bitcoin ETFs , which concern funds holding the asset itself. Selling a company’s stock changes its shareholder register; it does not directly transfer coins out of its treasury. The next useful evidence will be the rebalance’s execution and subsequent financing disclosures. Until then, claims that the deletion guarantees a Bitcoin liquidation, or has no possible economic effect, both reach beyond what the announcement establishes. written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Data.title: From Martinique to the Canary Islands: Nexo Card Follows Crypto Holders on Holiday
Data.body: Crypto holders like to travel, and now their card can follow them to the beach. Nexo has expanded its Nexo Card to a string of overseas territories and autonomous regions across France, Spain and Finland. The move coincides with the release of its report Digital assets and the European lifestyle , which finds that travel is one of the biggest and fastest-growing ways European cardholders spend their digital asset wealth. The new destinations The card is now available in: France: Réunion, Martinique, Guadeloupe, French Guiana, Mayotte and Saint-Martin Spain: the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla Finland: the Åland Islands Many of these are among the extended European region's most popular holiday spots, from the year-round sun of the Canaries to the Caribbean beaches of the French Antilles. "This expansion brings the Nexo Card directly to popular travel destinations across the extended European region," said Yasen Yankov, Head of Product Management at Nexo. Why travel matters The timing is backed by the numbers. According to the report, travel was the second-largest spending category on the Nexo Card in 2025, accounting for 15.9% of volume. Travel spending also grew 22% compared with 2024. More broadly, nearly a third of all spending on the card went on travel, eating out and leisure. Restaurants took 88.5% of food and drink spending, a sign that cardholders are paying for experiences as much as for goods. Europe is a natural market for this. The region captured about $2 trillion of the $6.15 trillion spent on leisure travel worldwide in 2025, roughly one third of the global total, according to the World Travel & Tourism Council. Bigger tickets, different funding Nexo cardholders in Europe spent about €80 per transaction in 2025, around twice the euro-area card average of about €38 reported by the European Central Bank. What sets that spending apart is how it is paid for. In credit mode, clients borrow against holdings such as Bitcoin and Ether rather than selling them. In debit mode, crypto is converted at the point of sale, with stablecoins making up 72.7% of that direct crypto spending. For a traveller, that means a hotel, a dinner or a boat trip can be paid for without first cashing out of digital assets. A wider shift The expansion arrives as crypto ownership keeps climbing in Europe. In early 2026, about one in five respondents in the Netherlands and one in six in Germany said they owned crypto assets, according to the Adan and Ipsos 2026 Barometer. In France, 53% of holders had already paid for something with crypto, most often by card. "We see digital asset wealth, made spendable by tools like the Nexo Card, becoming a new driver of consumption," Yankov said. Nexo describes the Nexo Card, which runs on the Mastercard network, as the first crypto card to combine credit and debit functions. Read the full report: Digital assets and the European lifestyle . Data.title: Nebius Stock Drops 12% Despite 571% Revenue Surge as AI Cloud Firm Cuts 2026 Outlook
Data.body: Key takeaways Nebius revenue surges 571% to nearly $981 million Delayed data center capacity weakens 2026 revenue outlook Capital spending forecast rises to $27 billion Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) shares dropped nearly 12% in premarket trading on November 12 despite the artificial intelligence cloud provider reporting a 571% increase in third-quarter revenue, as delayed computing capacity forced management to lower its 2026 revenue expectations. According to the company's official earnings release , revenue reached $980.8 million, up from $146.1 million a year earlier and above Wall Street expectations of approximately $908 million. Nebius Revenue Jumps 571% as AI Cloud Demand Accelerates Nebius reported AI cloud revenue of $973.8 million, representing approximately 99% of total quarterly sales and a 643% annual increase. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $6.4 billion at September's end, more than doubling from $3 billion in June. However, approximately $325 million in quarterly revenue came from nonrecurring arrangements involving deployment of Nebius technology on third-party infrastructure. This distinction matters because the contribution boosted reported growth without necessarily representing recurring cloud consumption. The latest results follow an earlier Nebius and CoreWeave comparison , which highlighted the growing importance of financing costs and infrastructure utilization for AI cloud providers. Nebius also reported $38.7 billion in remaining performance obligations, reflecting substantial contracted future business. Why Is Nebius Stock Falling After Strong Earnings? The company's shareholder letter explains that some third-party computing capacity expected to become operational in 2026 has been delayed until the first half of 2027. Consequently, Nebius now expects annual revenue near the bottom of its previous $3 billion–$3.4 billion forecast. Management also pushed back its target of exceeding $7 billion in annualized revenue run rate from December to February. Meanwhile, its 2026 capital expenditure forecast increased from $20 billion–$25 billion to approximately $27 billion. The larger spending commitment reinforces concerns raised when Nebius returned to debt markets to finance its rapidly expanding AI infrastructure. Despite the revised near-term guidance, management expects 2027 revenue of $12 billion–$13 billion, with capital expenditures reaching $40 billion–$45 billion. Can Nvidia-Backed Nebius Finance Its Expansion? Nebius expects customer prepayments and asset-backed financing to cover approximately 75%–85% of its 2027 capital spending. That financing strategy follows Nvidia's $2 billion investment in the company earlier this year. Nevertheless, heavy capital requirements remain a central concern across AI infrastructure businesses. Rival CoreWeave recently reported 168% quarterly revenue growth , although its borrowing costs and debt obligations continued increasing. The wider AI infrastructure financing debate has intensified as investors question whether long-term contracts can translate into sustainable earnings quickly enough.

Data.title: Bitcoin Falls Alongside Nvidia as ETF Outflows Reach $1.44 Billion
Data.body: Bitcoin falls alongside Nvidia on Thursday as renewed selling in technology stocks weighed on risk assets, while persistent withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds added further pressure to the market. BTC slipped approximately 0.7% from midnight UTC, trading around $73,400 and hovering close to its daily low. Ethereum also weakened, falling around 0.5% to approximately $2,044. The latest move followed a sharp drop in Nvidia shares during pre-market trading. The combination of technology-sector weakness and continued institutional withdrawals has left Bitcoin struggling to regain momentum, despite a partial recovery in equities earlier in the week. Nvidia Sell-Off Spills Over Into Crypto Markets Nvidia became a major focus for investors after reports raised questions about the company’s leadership. The New York Times reported on an alleged relationship involving CEO Jensen Huang and a company executive, while The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove him. Nvidia shares fell approximately 7% in pre-market trading following the reports. The company had not announced any decision regarding Huang at the time of publication. The uncertainty also affected broader technology markets. Nasdaq-100 futures declined around 0.6%, giving back part of the gains recorded on Wednesday after AI cloud-computing company CoreWeave delivered stronger-than-expected earnings. Bitcoin’s reaction highlights the close relationship that can develop between cryptocurrencies and high-growth technology stocks during periods of heightened risk aversion. When investors reduce exposure to technology and AI-related companies, digital assets can face similar selling pressure. The decentralized GPU network Render also moved lower, declining approximately 3.1% as Nvidia’s weakness weighed on sentiment across the AI-related investment theme. Bitcoin ETF Outflows Extend to Fifth Consecutive Day Institutional fund flows are providing another challenge for Bitcoin. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $299.9 million in net outflows on Wednesday, according to SoSoValue, extending their withdrawal streak to five consecutive sessions. Cumulative outflows since November 5 have now reached approximately $1.44 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $269.7 million of Wednesday’s withdrawals. The fund has now recorded nine consecutive sessions of net redemptions, indicating that selling pressure is not limited to smaller investment products. Continued ETF withdrawals are important because these funds have become a significant channel for institutional exposure to Bitcoin. Persistent redemptions can weaken demand for the asset and make it more difficult for buyers to absorb selling pressure. Fed Expectations and Economic Data Keep Traders Cautious Beyond Nvidia and ETF flows, investors are also monitoring the outlook for US monetary policy. The Federal Reserve is scheduled to meet on December 8–9, with CME FedWatch data indicating that markets were pricing in approximately a 90% probability of an interest rate increase. Higher borrowing costs can weigh on assets such as Bitcoin by tightening financial conditions and reducing the appeal of investments that do not generate traditional interest income. Traders were also awaiting the latest initial jobless claims figures, while Nvidia’s board decisions remained another potential source of market volatility. Bitcoin Faces Renewed Pressure Near $73,000 Bitcoin’s move toward $73,400 leaves the cryptocurrency struggling to establish a convincing recovery after its recent decline. The market is facing pressure from several directions, including technology-sector uncertainty, persistent ETF withdrawals, and expectations of tighter monetary policy. The $73,000 area is an important near-term level to monitor as BTC trades close to its daily low. A sustained move lower could reinforce bearish sentiment, particularly if institutional outflows continue. On the other hand, a recovery in technology stocks and a slowdown in ETF redemptions could help stabilize demand. For now, however, neither development has provided a clear signal that selling pressure is fading. Will Bitcoin manage to defend the $73,000 area as Nvidia shares remain under pressure? And could another week of ETF outflows push BTC toward lower support levels?
